title: WPPIL/137/2018 of AJAY GAUTAM Vs UNION OF INDIA

paras.text:
THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (PIL) No. 137 of 2018
Ajay Gautam .....Petitioner
Vs.
Union of India & others ...Respondents
Present:
Mr. Ajay Veer Pundir, Amicus Curiae for the petitioner.
Mr. Sanjay Bhatt, Standing Counsel for Union of India/respondent no. 1.
Mr. Pradeep Joshi, Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand.
Ms. Sakshi Popli and Mr. Ashutosh Posti, Advocate for respondent no. 6.
Dated: 6th March, 2019
Coram: Hon'ble Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.
 Hon'ble N.S. Dhanik, J.
Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J. (Oral)
 The counter affidavit, filed on behalf of respondent
nos. 2 & 3, is taken on record.
 A letter addressed by Sri Ajay Gautam has been
treated as a writ petition. In the said letter Sri Ajay Gautam
states that the failure of various State Governments to take
necessary steps has resulted in contamination of the River
Ganges rendering it unsafe for performance of religious rituals
by Hindus; and, on account of water being stored in two major
dams (Alaknanda & Tehri), there is depletion in flow of water
into the River Ganges, more particularly at religious places like
Haridwar, Rishikesh etc. On the basis of the said letter, the
reliefs sought for therein have been classified separately, and
are as detailed in prayers b, c & d which read as under:
"b. Issue an appropriate direction to the State of
Uttarakhand & Union of India to maintain quality
of water at least to the extent it is safe for
performing religious rituals by Hidus ad
followers of other religions, in rivers Maa Ganga
and Maa Yamuna and their tributaries.
 c. Issue an appropriate direction to the State of
Uttarakhand and Union of India to
release/maintain of sufficient flow of water in the
above named rivers (throughout the year) so that

2
worshipers/believers/Hindus can perform
various rituals including last rite and rituals after
last rite of the worshipers/believers/Hindus.
d. Issue an appropriate direction to the State of
Uttarakhand and Union of India to
release/maintain sufficient flow of water in the
above named rivers (throughout the year) so that
rivers are rejuvenated & are fit for performing
various rituals by the worshipers/ believers/
Hindus like Aachmen to Snaan ( Shodash Senskar
Etc.)"
In so far as prayer (b) is concerned, the State of
Uttarakhand has filed a detailed counter affidavit regarding the
measures taken by them for waste water management, and
have furnished details of the status of sewage generation and
its treatment at Haridwar, Rishikesh, Muni-ki-Reti, Tapovan,
Devprayag, Kirtinagar, Srinagar, Rudraprayag, Karanprayag,
Nandprayag, Gopeshwar-Chamoli, Joshimath, Badrinath,
Uttarkashi & Gauchar. The counter affidavit also details the
steps taken by the Government for construction of Ghats and
crematoria; regarding forestry intervention, and to control
pollution in the River Yamuna also.
From the counter affidavit, it does appear that
some steps have been taken by the State of Uttarakhand to
improve the quality of the water in the River Ganges. As the
Court lacks expertise, in such matters, the question, whether
the steps taken by the State Government would suffice to
improve the quality of water in the River Ganges, to the
standards sought for by the petitioner for performing religious
rituals, are incapable of specific determination in proceedings
under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
Suffice it to direct the State Government to
continue their efforts in ensuring that the quality of the water in
the river ganges is improved, if possible, to the extent it is
capable of being used for performing religious rituals. Prayer
(c) and (d) would require this Court to regulate the storage of

3
water in the dams in Uttarakhand, and its periodical discharge.
Water is stored in these dams to cater to the irrigation needs of
the people of the State, besides generation of electricity. Issues
such as how much water should be stored in these dams, how
much should be discharged and when, are again matters in the
executive realm, and are all matters regarding which this Court
lacks expertise. Suffice it, in such circumstances, to dispose of
the writ petition directing the State of Uttarakhand to take all
such measures as are necessary to maintain the purity of the
River Ganges.
Miscellaneous application (IA No. 2555/2019)
stands disposed of. No costs.
 (N.S. Dhanik, J.) (Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.)
 06.03.2019
A.kaur
